# Class field layouts and suspendable method dispatch (SIM-011)

The task module runs every positive fixture through the public CLI in both HDL
optimizer modes on legacy, compact/portable and compact/GMP values (GMP when
`LLG_TEST_GMP_ROOT` is set). Expected outputs are derived by hand from the
cited clauses (IEEE 1800-2009 Clause 8, §§6.21-6.22, 13.3-13.5), not captured
from llg. Times are printed with `%0d $time` in the default 1 ns unit.

| Fixture | Clause and independent oracle |
| --- | --- |
| `timed_virtual` | §§8.20, 13.3, 13.5. `b` holds a `Derived`, so `b.run(4, o, r)` selects `Derived::run`: after `#2` `count` = 4 and `tag` = `dx`, the output `o` = 4 * 10 + 5 = 45 is copied out at return and the `ref` `r` = 7 + 100 = 107 at once; after `#3` the inherited real `scale` = 1.5 * 2 = 3.00; time 5 (`A`). `Quick::run` has no timing: `o` = -3, `r` = 214 at time 5 (`B`). A plain `Base` runs `Base::run`: `#1`, `o` = 2, `r` = 215 at time 6 (`C`). `drive` passes a `Chain` as its `Base` formal; `Chain::run` calls `super.run`, i.e. `Derived::run` (5 time units, `count` = 1, `tag` = `dx`, `o` = 15, `r` = 315), then `#1 o = 16`: `drive t=12 n=1 lo=16 r=315`, and the object shows `count=1 tag=dx scale=3.00` (`D`). |
| `witness_timed_class` | Adopted FND-002 witness `timed_class` (ledger L-F09-07-03, L-F12-01-02): the `Expected:` header gives `class` after the method's `#1`. |
| `hierarchical_tasks` | §§8.15, 8.10, 23.6. `Der::step` runs `super.step()` (`#1`, `x` = 1), `#2 x = 11`, then the module task `tb.note(11)` (`#1`, `log_v` = 11): time 4. The static task `Base::s_wait(3)` ends at 7. |
| `receiver_rebind` | §8.20. `h.hold(seen)` is called on object 1 (`O`), which is selected at the call. At 2 the parallel branch rebinds `h` to a new `P` with `id` 2. At 5 the running activation still reads its own object: `seen` = 1 and object 1's `id` becomes 2; `h` names the `P` (`id` 2): `t=5 seen=1 first=2 h=2 same=0`. The next call through `h` selects `P::hold`: at 10 `seen` = 200 and `id` = 12. |
| `automatic_methods` | §§8.6, 13.3.1 (class methods are automatic). Three concurrent `work` activations keep their own `acc`: `a.work(3, 1)` = 1 + 100 = 101, `a.work(1, 2)` = 102, `b.work(2, 3)` = 203; the join ends at 3 and the static `calls` counted 3. `fact(5)` recurses to 120. `count_down(3)` recurses three levels with one `#1` each, so every level prints at 6; the innermost prints first: sums 1, 3, 6. |
| `static_specializations` | §§8.9, 8.10, 8.25. `Counter#(4)` and `Counter#(8)` are distinct classes with their own statics: two `Counter#(4)` objects and one `Counter#(8)` give `c4=2 c8=1`. `bump(1)` (time 1) and `bump(5)` (time 2), then two `Counter#(4)` bumps in parallel, one through the class scope and one through an instance (time 3): `tot4` = 10 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 16, `tot8` = 10 + 5 = 15. `v = '1` fills 4 and 8 bits: 15 and 255. |
| `handle_chains` | §§8.4, 8.8, 8.9, Table 6-7. `n1.next.val` is `n2.val` and `n1.next.next.val` is `n3.val`: `1 2 3`; writes through the chains reach `n2` and `n3`: `1 20 30`. String, real and method selections use `n2` and `n3`: names `n2 n3`, `r` = 2 * 0.5 = 1.0, `get` = 20 and 30. Writes through `n1.next` set `n2.name` = `two` and `n2.r` = 9.5; the uninitialized real is 0.0. The static handle `Node::head` = `n2`: `20 n3`; a write through it sets `n2.val` = 22. Each `Node` builds its own `Leaf` (`v` = 4), so `n1.leaf != n2.leaf`; `n1.next.leaf.v = 44` changes only `n2`'s: `44 4`. |
| `task_local_handles` | §§8.4, 9.3.2, 13.3.1. The automatic task's handle local reads `id` 1, then 2 after `#1` with `nm` = `p` and `get` = 2 at time 1; the joined branch reads 2 at 2 and writes 3, which the task sees after the join. The handle formal `f` reads `id` 5 at 3 and the joined branch writes `nm` = `q` at 4. The function's local handle gives 7 + 1 = 8. |
| `container_properties` | §§8.5, 8.8, 7.4-7.10. Each `Bag` initializes its own `q` = {1, 2}, `fixed` = {7, 8, 9} and `names` = {`x`, `y`}: `2 2 9 3 xy`. Writes through `a` and through the chain `a.next` reach `a`'s and `b`'s storage: `a.q` = {1, 2, 3}, `b.q` = {0, 1, 2}, `a.total()` = 7 + 80 + 9 + 1 + 2 + 3 = 102, `a.nib[1]` = `a` and the unwritten `a.nib[0]` is the 4-state default `x`, `b.names[1]` = `z`, `b.aa["k"]` = 5, `b.d` has 4 elements and `a.aa` none. `a.fill(2)` appends 0 and 10 one time unit apart: `t=2 5 0 10`. `b.steal(a)` pops `a.q`'s front 1 into `b.q` through the formal handle: `a.q` = {2, 3, 0, 10}, `b.q` = {0, 1, 2, 1}: `4 2 4 1`. The specializations `Holder#(byte, 3)` and `Holder#(string)` hold 3 and 2 elements: `100 hi 3 2`. |
| `packed_properties` | §§7.2, 8.4, 8.8, 11.5.1, 6.8 Table 6-7. The unpacked record `rec` defaults its `int` member to 0 and its `logic` member to `xxxx`; `init_rec` takes its pattern per object (`a` = 5, `c[1]` = 2); an uninitialized `int` property is 0: `0 xxxx 5 2 0`. Through the handle, `pk` = {8'h12, 4'h3} then `pk.a` = 8'h55 gives 12'h553; `v` = 0, `v[3:0]` = f, `v[7]` = 1 gives `10001111`. `setb` writes `pk.b` = 9 (12'h559), `rec.c[1]` = 7 and `v[0]` (already 1). Writes through the chain `n.next` reach `m`: `42 a 9`, while `n.rec.a` stays 0. Copying `n.init_rec` into `m.rec` gives `5 6 2` and the two compare equal (1). |
| `record_properties` | §§7.2, 8.4, 8.8. Each object's `rec` starts as {`r`, 2, 0.5} and `blank` as {``, 0, 0.0}; `n1.rec.n` becomes 3: `r 3 0.50 [] 0`. `bump` makes {`r+`, 4}: tags `r+4` and `r2` (`n2` untouched). The chain `n1.next` writes `n2.rec.s` = `two`; `n2.blank` receives a copy of `n1.rec` through a module record; `n2.slow()` multiplies `n2.rec.r` by 4 after `#1`: `t=1 two r+ 4 2.00`, and `n2.blank == n1.rec` is 1. |
| `null_receiver` | §8.4. `h` is null at time 1: the task call is a run-time error reported at its source position (`tb:15:12`); the process stops, so `after` is not printed and the run fails. |
| `null_property` | §8.4. Writing `h.id` through a null handle is a run-time error at `tb:15:9`; `after` is not printed. |
| `bad_downcast` | §8.16. The function form of `$cast` from a plain `A` to `B` returns 0 and leaves `derived` unchanged: `fn=0 same=1`; from an `A` handle holding a `B` it succeeds: `ok=1 b=2`. The task form with an incompatible source is a run-time error at `tb:25:9` and leaves `derived` unchanged: `after same=1`. |
| `neg_local_access` | Nearest illegal form (§8.18): a `local` property accessed outside its class is a frontend error. |
| `neg_protected_access` | Nearest illegal form (§8.18): a `protected` property accessed outside the class hierarchy is a frontend error. |
| `neg_abstract_new` | Nearest illegal form (§8.21): constructing an abstract class is a frontend error. |
| `method_forks` | §§8.11, 8.20, 9.3.2. `run`'s first branch calls `this.bump(1)`, which uses `worker::scale`: `n` = 10 at 1, then its nested branch increments `n` at 2 and the first branch ends, completing the `join_any`: `any 11 at 2`. The second branch prints at 5 and `wait fork` returns: `seen 11`, `all 11 at 5`. `detached` starts at 5; its branch sets `n` = 30 at 6 (`branch 3`) and the method reads it at 7: `detached 3 n 30`. In `joined` (from 7) one branch increments at 8 and the other's `bump(1)` adds 10 at 10: `joined 41 at 10`. |
| `neg_const_assign` | Nearest illegal form (§8.19): assigning a `const` property in a method other than the constructor is a frontend error. |
| `neg_record_container_property` | Legal by §§7.2, 8.4; a record property with a queue member would need per-object companion containers and is rejected explicitly. |
| `neg_multidim_property` | Legal by §§7.4.2, 8.4; a multidimensional fixed-array property is rejected explicitly (one-dimensional ones are per-object containers). |
| `neg_static_record_property` | Legal by §8.9; a static record property with a string member is rejected explicitly (instance ones are per-object values). |
